item.title: [Featured Article] Indiana-class battleship
item.description: The Indiana class was a class of three pre-dreadnought battleships launched in 1893. These were the first battleships built by the United States Navy comparable to contemporary European ships, such as the British HMS Hood. Authorized in 1890 and commissioned between November 1895 and April 1896, these were relatively small battleships with heavy armor and ordnance that pioneered the use of an intermediate battery. Specifically intended for coastal defense, their freeboard was insufficient to deal well with the waves of the open ocean. The turrets lacked counterweights, and the main belt armor was placed too low to be effective under most conditions.

item.title: [In the News] In association football, the Court of Arbitration for Sport restores Senegal as the winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, overturning the Confederation of African Football's decision to declare Morocco as the winner of the tournament.
item.description: The 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final was a football match played on 18 January 2026 at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, Morocco. It determined the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), the 35th edition of the biennial African tournament organised by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), and was contested between Senegal and hosts Morocco.

item.title: [In the News] Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after a scandal in which he was allegedly targeted by a Chinese spy and had extramarital affairs.
item.description: Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang is a Taiwanese and American electrical engineer and business executive who is the co-founder, president, and chief executive officer (CEO) of Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies. As of November 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at US$143.4 billion, making him the 13th-wealthiest person in the world.

item.title: [In the News] The joint ESA–JAXA mission BepiColombo enters orbit around Mercury.
item.description: BepiColombo is a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) which, in 2026, became the second mission ever to enter orbit around the planet Mercury, the first being MESSENGER. It comprises two orbiters: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), built and operated by ESA, and Mio, built and operated by JAXA. Together the spacecraft will perform a comprehensive study of Mercury, including characterization of its magnetic field, magnetosphere, and both interior and surface structure.

item.title: [In the News] Mathematician Levent Alpöge, working with the AI model Claude, announces a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis.
item.description: In mathematics, the Riemann hypothesis is the theorem that the Riemann zeta function has its zeros only at the negative even integers and at complex numbers with real part. First posed in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, pure mathematicians considered the hypothesis to be one of the most important problems in the field. It is important in number theory because it implies bounds on the distribution of prime numbers. The name is also used for some closely related analogues such as the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields, which was proved by André Weil around 1940.

item.title: [Most Read #1] Joe Milton
item.description: Daily Views: 385,182 — Joseph Jay Milton III is an American professional football quarterback for the Philadelphia Eagles of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football for the Michigan Wolverines and Tennessee Volunteers before being selected by the New England Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft. He has also played for the Dallas Cowboys.

item.title: [Most Read #2] Ramayana: Part 1
item.description: Daily Views: 229,774 — Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the Hindu epic Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first instalment of a two-part film series, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana, which chronicle the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The first part features an ensemble cast that includes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Lara Dutta, Shobana, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Arun Govil, Adinath Kothare.

item.title: [Most Read #4] Mason Rudolph (American football)
item.description: Daily Views: 117,924 — Brett Mason Rudolph III is an American professional football quarterback for the Pittsburgh Steelers of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football for the Oklahoma State Cowboys, winning the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award during his last year before being selected by the Steelers in the third round of the 2018 NFL draft. Rudolph has also played for the Tennessee Titans.

item.title: [Most Read #5] Elizabeth Holmes
item.description: Daily Views: 117,706 — Elizabeth Anne Holmes is an American businesswoman convicted of fraud in connection with her health technology company Theranos. Holmes founded Theranos in 2003, and its valuation soared in the early 2010s after it claimed to have revolutionized blood testing by developing methods that needed only very small volumes of blood, such as from a fingerprick. In 2015, Forbes named Holmes the youngest and wealthiest self-made female billionaire in the United States on the basis of a $9 billion valuation of Theranos. In the following year, as accusations of fraud about Theranos's claims began to surface, Forbes revised its estimate of Holmes's net worth to zero, and Fortune named her in its feature article on "The World's 19 Most Disappointing Leaders".

item.title: [Most Read #6] List of highest-grossing Indian films
item.description: Daily Views: 116,885 — This ranking lists the highest-grossing Indian films produced by Indian cinema, based on conservative global box office estimates as reported by organisations classified as green by Wikipedia. The figures are not adjusted for inflation. However, there is no official tracking of figures and sources publishing data are frequently pressured to increase their estimates.

item.title: [Most Read #7] Ansel Adams
item.description: Daily Views: 111,201 — Ansel Easton Adams was an American landscape photographer and environmentalist who was known for his black-and-white photographs of the American West. He helped found Group f/64, an association of photographers advocating "pure" photography which favored sharp focus and the use of the full tonal range of a photograph. He and Fred Archer developed a system of image-making called the Zone System, a method of achieving a desired final print through a technical understanding of how the tonal range of an image is the result of choices made in exposure, negative development, and printing.

item.title: [Most Read #8] Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Daily Views: 110,558 — Aaron Charles Rodgers is an American professional football quarterback. He played college football for the California Golden Bears, setting the school's record for lowest single-season and career interception rates before being selected by the Green Bay Packers in the first round of the 2005 NFL draft. After backing up Brett Favre for the first three years of his NFL career, Rodgers became the Packers' starting quarterback in 2008. In the 2010 season, he led them to a victory in Super Bowl XLV, earning the Super Bowl MVP. He was named Associated Press Athlete of the Year in 2011, was voted league MVP by the Associated Press for the 2011, 2014, 2020, and 2021 NFL seasons and is a four-time winner of the Best NFL Player ESPY Award. Rodgers is regarded as one of the greatest and most talented quarterbacks of all time.

item.title: [Most Read #9] Grand Theft Auto VI
item.description: Daily Views: 109,088 — Grand Theft Auto VI is a 2026 action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games. It is the eighth main entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V, and the sixteenth entry overall. Set in the fictional US state of Leonida, based on Florida, the story follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they lead a life of crime to secure a better life. Along the way, they uncover a state-wide criminal conspiracy involving corrupt police officers. The game's open world allows players to freely roam Leonida and its Miami-inspired Vice City and engage in various side activities.

item.title: [Most Read #10] The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
item.description: Daily Views: 96,530 — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a 2026 American dystopian film produced and directed by Francis Lawrence from a screenplay by Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie. Based on the 2025 novel Sunrise on the Reaping by Suzanne Collins, it is the sixth installment in The Hunger Games film series, serving as the second prequel to The Hunger Games (2012) after The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023).
